options: Severe pain out of proportion to a soft belly
Recurrent self-limiting attacks since youth, 1–3 days each
Alternating habit, pain relieved by defecation
Vomiting with the diarrhoea (others at home affected)
Recurrent short fevers with each pain attack (family members similar)
Diabetic — missed insulin or intercurrent illness
Pain after meals with fear of eating and weight loss (elderly, vascular disease)
Nausea and appetite loss preceding the pain

history.ask: Menstrual / obstetric status (women of childbearing age)

options: Family members with recurrent fever-and-pain attacks (FMF)
Family history of inflammatory bowel disease

red_flags: Rigid abdomen, rebound tenderness, or absent bowel sounds — surgical abdomen, refer immediately
Severe pain out of proportion to examination in an elderly or atrial-fibrillation patient (mesenteric ischaemia)
Hypotension, tachycardia, or cold peripheries with abdominal pain
Haematemesis, melaena, or bloody diarrhoea with fever
Missed period with acute lower abdominal pain — ectopic pregnancy until excluded
Diabetic with vomiting, deep sighing breathing, or drowsiness (DKA)
Anuria, or colic with fever and rigors (obstructed infected kidney)
exam: Record full vitals — fever, tachycardia, hypotension, and deep sighing (Kussmaul) breathing each redirect the pathway
Inspect for jaundice, dehydration (dry tongue, skin turgor), and pallor
Auscultate bowel sounds BEFORE palpation — silent abdomen or high-pitched tinkling changes everything
Palpate all quadrants starting away from the pain — localise tenderness, guarding, rigidity, rebound
Palpate specifically for masses, hepatomegaly, and a distended bladder
Perform Murphy's manoeuvre for right-upper-quadrant pain
Percuss the renal angles for tenderness (pyelonephritis, obstructed stone)
Watch the patient during a colic wave — a restless rolling patient suggests stone; a still patient guarding suggests peritoneal irritation
Perform a digital rectal exam when bleeding, severe constipation, or diarrhoea needs characterising
Smell the breath for ketones and check a fingerstick glucose in any diabetic with pain
Examine hernial orifices — an obstructed hernia mimics medical colic
Check the skin over the painful area for vesicular zoster rash before it declares itself

investigations.why: Haematuria supports ureteric stone; pyuria and nitrites rule in UTI/pyelonephritis; ketones and glucose flag DKA — one strip test arbitrates three differentials

investigations.test: Random blood glucose (fingerstick immediately if diabetic)
investigations.why: Rules DKA in or out at the bedside in any diabetic with pain and vomiting — DKA is the abdominal pain that must never reach a surgeon

Marked leukocytosis supports pyelonephritis, mesenteric ischaemia, or a surgical cause over IBS and constipation; anaemia raises bleeding ulcer or malignancy; leukocytosis also accompanies FMF attacks
Dehydration from gastroenteritis, obstruction of a solitary kidney by stone, and DKA all declare themselves here; potassium guides safety before fluids in DKA
Raised transaminases with bilirubin support acute hepatitis for right-upper-quadrant pain; raised lipase rules in pancreatitis before any surgical referral for epigastric pain
High values push toward inflammatory/infective causes (pyelonephritis, IBD flare, FMF attack, ischaemia); a normal CRP after 12–24 h of pain argues against them and supports IBS or constipation

investigations.test: Pregnancy test (all women of childbearing age)
investigations.why: Non-negotiable before imaging or referral — a positive test with lower abdominal pain makes ectopic pregnancy the working diagnosis
First-line imaging: hydronephrosis (obstructing stone), gallbladder and liver disease, free fluid, appendiceal mass — directs whether the patient stays medical or crosses to surgery
Ova/parasites and pus cells characterise infective gastroenteritis; occult blood or pus supports IBD over IBS in chronic diarrhoea

investigations.test: CT abdomen with contrast (CT angiography if ischaemia suspected)
investigations.why: Second-line — when ultrasound is inconclusive, or urgently when mesenteric ischaemia is suspected (pain out of proportion in elderly/AF): rules vascular occlusion and deep pathology in or out
